summary_en: ROE targets revised: 5%+ medium-term, 8%+ long-term (vs. assumed cost of capital 8%). FY8/24 ROE −26.0% due to ¥2.3B impairment loss on fixed assets. Focus on existing business profitability improvement, selective M&A, capital-efficient investment above cost of capital. Training participation target raised to 90%+.
title_en: Response to Realizing Management with Awareness of Cost of Capital and Stock Price (Update)
translation_en_brief: Fujipream Corporation updated its capital-allocation and shareholder-return framework on 24 June 2024, following an initial disclosure on 1 May 2023. The company restated its analysis of operating and financial performance over the past five fiscal years (FY4/22–FY8/24). Recent metrics show sharp deterioration: sales fell from ¥19.2B (FY4/22) to ¥8.1B (FY8/24); FY8/24 recorded a ¥2.3B net loss (attributable to parent shareholders) due to impairment charges on fixed assets, pushing ROE to −26.0%. PBR remained above 1.0× except FY7/23 (0.98×) and stood at 1.42× as of FY8/24. The company views this multiple as reflecting both market confidence in its business foundation and expectations of recovery. However, ROE at 2.6% in FY7/23 and −26.0% in FY8/24 falls substantially below the company's assumed cost of capital of 8%, signalling a core concern. The company targets ROE improvement to 5%+ over the medium term and 8%+ long-term through three initiatives: (i) earnings lift in existing operations via manufacturing-cost reduction, SG&A optimization, and DX-driven productivity; human capital development (training participation target raised to 90%+); (ii) selective M&A and R&D investment leveraging existing technology and customer synergies, funded from cash generation; and (iii) capital-efficient management, requiring investment projects to exceed cost of capital and periodic validation of holdings and cash deployment. These actions target simultaneous profit growth and capital-efficiency improvement to sustain enterprise value.
